units.translation: the all-true, evil-prophesying Erinys, invoked by my father's prayers
if a god grants it well, altogether truly

where M has παναρκεῖς [all-sufficient], but with λ written above by a very recent hand, i.e. παναλκεῖς [all-powerful], which is in the copies. The scholiast read παναρκεῖς [all-sufficient], explaining it as κατὰ πάντα βοηθοί [helpers in all things]; for this is proper to the gods.
helpers in all things; for this is proper to the gods
a great net of slavery, of all-catching ruin

Ch. 70 διαλγὴς δ᾽ ἄτα διαφέρει τὸν αἴτιον παναρκέτας νόσου βρύειν. The corruption is evident: for a word of cretic measure is required. The scholiast did not notice this, explaining it as τῆς εἰς πάντα τὸν χρόνον ἀρκούσης αὐτῷ.
grievous ruin carries the guilty one to abound in all-sufficient disease
sufficient for him for all time
is in M for πάνδυρτε [all-lamented], which see.
O my wholly lamentable race of Oedipus
where Blomfield rightly has πανδαμὶ, πανομιλί. πανδημί [with the whole people, with the whole host] Aldus and Robortellus.
The Doric form is preserved in M in the second place,
For some go against the towers with the whole people, with the whole host
and keep holy silence with the whole people
with the whole people, with the whole host
where πανδημίᾳ [with the whole people] is used adverbially for πανδημί [with the whole people].
For the whole people with right hands made the air bristle

where in M βουνῖτι ἔνδικον [hill, just], which Paleius corrected from the scholiast's note, who interprets it as δικαία σέβεσθαι, ἢ ἢν δικαίως πάντες τιμῶσιν [just to revere, or whom all justly honor].
O hill of earth, wholly just object of reverence
just to revere, or whom all justly honor
where M in the first hand has πανδίκους [wholly just], but ou changed to w by the same or another ancient hand.
Hear, maidens, hear my wholly just, hand-voted prayers
and she is wholly justly hated
For I wholly justly promise you
become a wholly just and pious protector
The scholiast explains it by ἐπιδεχομένη [receiving] or ὑποδεχομένη [receiving].
receiving all the burden of education
into the all-receiving and unseen land
in the all-receiving halls of strangers
In both places M has πανόδυρτον [all-lamented], which Blomfield corrected.
Thus Ritschl for πανδάκρυτε [all-tearful], for which πολυδάκρυτε [much-tearful] is substituted in many copies.
I will send forth also wholly lamentable
Alas, alas, you wholly lamentable one
having established common contests in the assembly, we will deliberate
